newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sees natural gas demand up by year 2000.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sees natural gas demand up by year 2000.

text.p: Bulgaria expects its natural gas demand to rise by five to eight percent a year until the end of the century, senior officials said on Wednesday.
They said they expected the country's gas consumption rise to eight billion cubic metres by the year 2000.
Bulgaria, which is poor in energy resources, is heavily dependent on annual imports of some five billion cubic metres a year from Russia.

Sofia receives gratis about five billion cubic metres annually from Russia under a bilateral agreement as compensation for its role in the construction of Russia's Yamburg gas field. The accord expires in 1997.
Under the same agreement, Bulgaria will purchase more than three billion cubic metres a year until 2010.
Bulgaria hopes to pay less for the Russian gas following the setting up of a gas joint stock company Topenergy with Russia's Gazprom.
Topenergy, which was set up in 1995, is awaiting a government decision on its application for a concession for a transit pipeline and other facilities.
Bulgarian state gas monopolist Bulgargaz and Topenergy plan to invest more than $570 million in the construction of 650 km of pipelines for the transit of Russian gas by 2010, energy officials said.

Bulgaria has a 2,000-km-long pipeline network, which includes 625-km transit pipelines, and Bulgargaz has invested $442 million in their construction, the company's deputy executive director Ivan Peichev told a Balkan gas conference in Sofia which ended on Tuesday.
Bulgaria, which is planning to become a Balkan gas distribution centre, is currently supplying Russian gas to Turkey only.
Greece said it would start filling its main pipeline with gas on Monday as it had completed the network's construction on its territory.
Bulgaria has also constructed and filled with gas a pipeline link with Macedonia and is waiting for its western neighbour to complete work on its pipeline.
Bulgaria plans to buld a pipeline for gas supplies to Serbia.
